lead.headline: Zay Flowers caught the lead, then fumbled it
lead.dek: Maye I touch your TDs? needed 11.65 from its last receiver Monday night. At 8:09 p.m. one catch put it ahead by 1.76. The fumble on the same play cost 2.0. Bad things man bad things wins by 0.24.
body: At 8:09 p.m. Monday, in the last NFL game of the week, Zay Flowers caught a 15-yard pass and Maye I touch your TDs? took the lead, 174.48 to 172.72. I’ve covered the defending champion for ten weeks. I had the headline typed. Then Flowers fumbled at the end of the same play, the other side recovered, and the 2.0-point fumble penalty dropped the champ to 172.48. Same snap, two lead changes. Final: Bad things man bad things 172.72, Maye I touch your TDs? 172.48. Lost by 0.24. That isn’t a margin. That’s a rounding error with a body count.

Here’s how it got to one snap. Bad things man bad things finished Sunday at 172.72 with nobody left. Maye entered Monday at 161.08 with Flowers to play, needing more than 11.64. Monday morning’s brief made the champ a 69.3% favorite. Flowers finished with 11.4. Without the fumble he finishes with 13.4, and the champ wins by 1.76.

Sunday was a street fight. Maye led by 35.72 at 10:17 a.m. behind Amon-Ra St. Brown’s two touchdowns, then the lead changed hands nine times between 11:13 a.m. and 12:36 p.m. Emmett Johnson, a Saturday 7:56 a.m. pickup, scored 35.1 and caught the 6-yard touchdown that flipped it at 12:28 p.m. Eight minutes later Bijan Robinson’s 3-yard touchdown flipped it back, and James Cook III’s 74-yard run at 12:51 p.m. pushed Bad things man bad things to its biggest lead, 26.56. Chuba Hubbard scored 34.2 and the Los Angeles Rams D/ST, a Wednesday 12:10 a.m. claim and the third time this franchise has added that defense, scored 17.0.

Now the part that’s going to sting. Omarion Hampton scored 17.5 on Maye’s bench, and he played in the same Monday night game as Flowers. Christian Watson started at flex and scored 6.7. That one swap is worth 10.8. The best lineup Maye could have set scored 183.28 and wins by 10.56. Week 8: lost by 1.58 with winning swaps on the bench. Week 9: lost by 6.12 with Breece Hall on the bench. Week 10: lost by 0.24 with Hampton on the bench. Three straight weeks the bench decided the game.

The champ scored 172.48, the fourth-best total in the league this week, and is 2-8. Its all-play record is 31-39; its luck rating is -2.4, the worst in the league. Its playoff odds went from 70.4% to 25.2% in one week. Bad things man bad things is 8-2, tied with Poochinski for first, with an 87.7% shot at a top-two seed. Its close-game record is 3-1. Maye’s is 2-5. Some teams are lucky. Some teams are owed money by the universe.

games.headline: Poochinski erases 53.0 and posts the week’s high
games.dek: Cherry Blossom led by 53.0 at 2:34 p.m. Sunday, set a perfect lineup and still lost 192.44 to 172.2. The five-game win streak is over.
body: At 2:34 p.m. Sunday, Christian McCaffrey caught a 74-yard touchdown and Cherry Blossom led Poochinski by 53.0. McCaffrey finished with 46.3. Parker Washington added 28.2 and Trevor Lawrence 27.78. Cherry Blossom left 0.0 points on its bench. Perfect lineup. And it lost by 20.24.

That’s because Poochinski’s Dallas stack showed up in the late window: Dak Prescott 35.42, CeeDee Lamb 20.2, Brandon Aubrey 11.0 and Javonte Williams 7.7, 74.32 in all. Jahmyr Gibbs had already scored 44.2 in the morning. At 4:42 p.m. Poochinski took the lead, 136.12 to 131.7, and never gave it back. Chase Brown’s 4-yard touchdown in the Sunday night game made it 174.58 to 164.8, and Poochinski’s lead peaked at 24.24 at 8:24 p.m.

Cherry Blossom entered Monday down 192.44 to 168.2 with only the Baltimore Ravens D/ST left. It scored 4.0. Poochinski’s 192.44 is the week’s high score, and Aaron Rodgers, added at 9:28 a.m. Sunday for Chris Godwin Jr., chipped in 15.62 at quarterback. Six moves all season, and the Sunday-morning one paid.

games.headline: deeboliciouskins wins by 54.84 with a bye starter
games.dek: George Pickens scored 43.5 a week after scoring zero. D’Andre Swift, on bye, scored zero. Big Stric Energy fell to 2-8.
body: Big Stric Energy led this game by 26.58 at 12:27 p.m. Sunday. Josh Allen scored 23.34, Nico Collins 24.4, and Allen’s 54-yard strike to Dalton Kincaid at 11:59 a.m. put Big Stric in front. Then Big Stric’s day ended at 123.24, the week’s low score, and deeboliciouskins’ afternoon began.

George Pickens, who scored 0.0 for this team in Week 9, scored 43.5 in Week 10. His 35-yard touchdown at 1:55 p.m. got deeboliciouskins close, and his 5-yard touchdown at 4:00 p.m. took the lead for good, 126.48 to 123.24. Patrick Mahomes added 35.42 and Ja’Marr Chase 34.1 on Sunday night. Final: 178.08 to 123.24, and the four-game losing streak is over.

It could have been much worse for Big Stric Energy. deeboliciouskins started D’Andre Swift on a bye and left 46.1 points on its bench, the most in the league. Its best lineup scored 224.18, more than anybody scored this week. Big Stric’s own best lineup, 138.34, still loses by about 40. Jalen Coker started and scored 0.3. DK Metcalf sat and scored 15.4. It didn’t matter. Nothing did.

games.headline: Santa Clara’s Finest never trails, AB81 never leads
games.dek: The Finest led by 116.3 on Sunday afternoon and won 190.86 to 140.42. AB81’s six-move Sunday shopping spree couldn’t close it.
body: Santa Clara’s Finest took the lead on its first play of Thursday night and kept it all week. AB81’s biggest lead was zero. By the end of Thursday, Cam Skattebo (27.2) and Isaiah Likely (27.7) had combined for 54.9, and both of Skattebo’s touchdowns came in that game. By 1:15 p.m. Sunday the lead was 116.3. That isn’t a deficit. That’s a forwarding address.

Joe Burrow scored 33.16, Blake Corum and Bhayshul Tuten went for 20.9 and 20.3, and Stefon Diggs added 20.3. The Finest left 0.0 points on the bench. Its 190.86 is a season high, the second-best score in the league this week, and it’s the second straight win.

AB81 entered Monday down 101.9 with Justin Herbert, Derrick Henry and Mark Andrews to play. They scored 51.46, including two Henry touchdowns. Final margin: 50.44. Jaxon Smith-Njigba’s 31.1 and Cam Little’s 19.0 kept it respectable. George Kittle’s 13.4 on the bench, behind Rhamondre Stevenson’s 1.5, did not.

beats.headline: First place, highest score, six moves
body: Poochinski scored 192.44, the most in the league, and came back from 53.0 down to do it. That is what a first-place team looks like: it doesn’t panic at 2:34 p.m., it waits for its Dallas stack.

It left 16.5 on the bench, mostly Quinshon Judkins’ 16.1 behind Javonte Williams’ 7.7 and Tyler Higbee’s 10.7 behind Sam LaPorta’s 2.6. In a 20.24-point win, that’s a note in the margin, not a headline.
8-2, first on points with 1,706.92, and a 98.5% chance at a top-two seed. Its all-play record is 47-23, the best in the league.
beats.insight: Find a defense. The Seattle Seahawks D/ST is on bye and the projected lineup has an empty DEF slot. Judkins, Jadarian Price and Higbee are on bye too, so Chase Brown moves to flex. Poochinski projects for 174.8 and is a 68% favorite over Santa Clara’s Finest.

beats.headline: Won by 0.24, and it counts the same
body: Bad things man bad things finished Sunday at 172.72, then spent Monday night watching one opposing receiver. It won by 0.24 on a fumble. Close-game record: 3-1. This franchise doesn’t win pretty. It wins.

The bench nearly cost it. Kirk Cousins scored 16.38 behind Tyler Shough’s 10.98, and Josh Downs, a Wednesday claim, scored 15.3 behind Tetairoa McMillan’s 6.5. That’s 14.2 left on the bench in a game decided by a quarter of a point.
Chuba Hubbard (34.2), James Cook III (21.7) and the Rams D/ST (17.0) carried it. 8-2, tied with Poochinski, and 29 moves this season.
beats.insight: Four starters are on bye: Matthew Golden, Bijan Robinson, Zach Charbonnet and the Rams D/ST, which leaves an empty FLEX and a 137.08 projection against Cherry Blossom (27.8% to win). Fill the flex and the defense on the wire, and start Cousins over Shough. Hubbard’s usage is climbing; ride him.

beats.headline: A perfect lineup and a loss
body: Cherry Blossom left 0.0 points on its bench. It led by 53.0 at 2:34 p.m. Sunday. Christian McCaffrey scored 46.3. It lost by 20.24. Sometimes the other team is just better on the day.
The five-game win streak is over. Travis Kelce (5.0) and Brock Bowers (3.8) combined for 8.8 at tight end and flex, which is where this one slipped.
5-5, fourth place, 182.97 a game over the last three weeks, and 99.9% playoff odds. This team is fine.
beats.insight: Start Jonah Coleman when he’s back from his bye. His opportunities jumped from 8.0 to 18.5 a game on a 72% snap share, and he projects for 17.05. Bowers’ opportunities fell from 10.3 to 5.5, so he’s the one to bench. Puka Nacua and Michael Penix Jr. are on bye, but Cherry Blossom has three quarterbacks available and is a 72.2% favorite.

beats.headline: Snapped the skid with a bye starter
body: deeboliciouskins won by 54.84 and I’m still mad at it. D’Andre Swift was on bye and in the lineup. He scored 0.0. DJ Moore scored 19.4 on the bench. A week ago it was George Pickens in the lineup for 0.0. Two weeks, two zeros.

It also sat Tony Pollard (23.9) and the Minnesota Vikings D/ST (21.0). The bench held 46.1 points, the most in the league. The best lineup scored 224.18, which would have been the high score of the week by 31.74.
None of it mattered against Big Stric Energy. Pickens 43.5, Mahomes 35.42, Chase 34.1. 5-5, losing streak over, playoff odds 100%.
beats.insight: Start Tony Pollard. He scored 23.9 on the bench this week. Jason Myers is on bye, so the projected lineup has an empty K slot; pick up a kicker. Then check every starter’s bye. deeboliciouskins is a 98.7% favorite over AB81, the biggest edge on next week’s board.

beats.headline: Fixed the quarterback, found a tight end
body: Two weeks ago this column was writing about Lamar Jackson scoring 0.0 two weeks in a row. On Wednesday Santa Clara’s Finest claimed Baker Mayfield and dropped Jackson. On Thursday at 4:17 p.m. it added Bryce Young, and at 4:19 p.m. Isaiah Likely. Both started. Likely scored 27.7.
The result: a wire-to-wire 190.86, the best score this franchise has posted all season, and 0.0 points on the bench.
3-7, two straight wins, sixth place, and playoff odds of 57.1%. That number was 5.6% a week ago.
beats.insight: Blake Corum and Denzel Boston are on bye, but there are no empty slots and three quarterbacks available. Start Garrett Wilson: his opportunities rose from 7.3 to 13.0 a game with a 37% target share. Santa Clara’s Finest projects for 155.75 and is a 32% underdog to Poochinski.

beats.headline: Six moves in nine minutes
body: AB81 never led this game. Not once. On Sunday afternoon, down big, the front office made six moves between 4:33 p.m. and 4:42 p.m. Justin Herbert (16.26) and Mark Andrews (16.2) paid. Mike Gesicki was on the roster for two minutes.
Kittle scored 13.4 on the bench behind Stevenson’s 1.5. Jaxon Smith-Njigba’s 31.1 was the bright spot. It’s the second straight loss.
7-3, third place, playoff odds 100%. Its all-play record is 30-40 and its luck rating is +2.7, the best in the league. Translation: this team has been winning games it had no business winning.
beats.insight: Next week is a fire drill. Matthew Stafford, Sam Darnold, Rhamondre Stevenson, Kyren Williams and Smith-Njigba are on bye, and the projected lineup has empty QB, WR and FLEX slots and a 78.28 projection. Herbert is the only quarterback available, so claim Cam Ward first. AB81 is a 1.3% underdog to deeboliciouskins.

beats.headline: Lost by 0.24. Bench had 10.8.
body: Maye I touch your TDs? scored 172.48 and lost by 0.24 on a Monday night fumble. Omarion Hampton scored 17.5 on its bench. Do the math. Actually, don’t.
There was good news buried in there. Emmett Johnson, added at 7:56 a.m. Saturday for Aaron Jones Sr., scored 35.1, the best pickup in the league. Brock Purdy scored 31.66. Drake Maye scored 3.02.
2-8, three straight losses, and playoff odds down to 25.2%. Four games left, and it needs all of them.
beats.insight: This is the worst bye week in the league: Drake Maye, Harold Fannin Jr., A.J. Brown, Drake London, Christian Watson and the Cleveland Browns D/ST are all out, leaving empty QB, TE and DEF slots and a 106.96 projection. Claim Cam Ward or J.J. McCarthy at quarterback. Keep starting Emmett Johnson: his snap share went from 26% to 59%.

beats.headline: Led by 26.58, finished last
body: Big Stric Energy led by 26.58 at 12:27 p.m. Sunday. It finished with 123.24, the week’s low score. That’s the season in one afternoon.
Josh Allen scored 23.34 and Nico Collins 24.4. Jalen Coker scored 0.3 in the lineup while DK Metcalf scored 15.4 on the bench. Braelon Allen scored 5.6.
2-8, last place, fewest points in the league, and playoff odds of 17.7%.
beats.insight: Jordan Love is on bye and the projected lineup has an empty QB slot. Claim a quarterback before anything else: Cam Ward projects for 17.09. Braelon Allen’s opportunities fell from 16.8 to 9.5 a game, so he’s a bench piece now. Big Stric Energy is a 77.4% favorite over Maye I touch your TDs?. Win that one.

smart_move.stat_label: Isaiah Likely, added Thursday at 4:19 p.m.
smart_move.headline: Santa Clara’s Finest finally went shopping
smart_move.dek: Mayfield on Wednesday, Young and Likely on Thursday afternoon. Playoff odds went from 5.6% to 57.1%.
body: For two weeks Santa Clara’s Finest started Lamar Jackson for 0.0 and had no backup quarterback. On Wednesday at 12:10 a.m. it finally claimed Baker Mayfield and dropped Jackson. Thursday afternoon it kept going: Bryce Young at 4:17 p.m. for Hunter Henry, Isaiah Likely at 4:19 p.m.

Both started in the Thursday night game. Young scored 8.1, which in a two-quarterback league beats the zero this team had been getting. Likely scored 27.7, the second-best pickup of the week. With Cam Skattebo, that Thursday duo produced 54.9 before anybody else in the league had played.

The Finest won 190.86 to 140.42, never trailed, left 0.0 on the bench, and climbed into sixth place. Its playoff odds went from 5.6% to 57.1%. That’s what three moves can do when they’re the right three.

dumb_move.stat_label: D’Andre Swift, started on a bye
dumb_move.headline: deeboliciouskins started a running back on bye
dumb_move.dek: D’Andre Swift was off all week. He was in the lineup anyway. DJ Moore’s 19.4 sat on the bench.
body: D’Andre Swift’s team didn’t play in Week 10. Swift was in deeboliciouskins’ starting lineup anyway, and scored what you score on a bye: 0.0. DJ Moore scored 19.4 on the bench. That’s 19.4 points given away for nothing.

It’s the second straight week. In Week 9 this team started George Pickens, who didn’t play, for 0.0 while Moore scored 6.6 on the bench. Then deeboliciouskins lost by 22.4. This week Pickens scored 43.5 and bailed out the front office that benched him by accident last week.
The win, 178.08 to 123.24, makes this a cheap lesson. Add Tony Pollard (23.9) and the Vikings D/ST (21.0) sitting on the bench and there was 46.1 left behind. In a playoff game, that is the season.

bench_beat.stat_label: Points on the bench in a 0.24-point loss
bench_beat.headline: Omarion Hampton would have won it
bench_beat.dek: One swap, worth 10.8, in a game lost by 0.24. The champ’s bench has now decided three straight games.
body: Maye I touch your TDs? started Christian Watson at flex. He scored 6.7. Omarion Hampton sat on the bench and scored 17.5. Swap them and the champ scores 183.28 and beats Bad things man bad things by 10.56.
Hampton played Monday night, in the same game as Zay Flowers. So the champ spent Monday needing 11.65 from one receiver while a running back on its own bench was scoring 17.5 in the same stadium.

Week 8: lost by 1.58. Week 9: lost by 6.12 with Breece Hall’s 11.7 on the bench. Week 10: lost by 0.24 with Hampton’s 17.5 on the bench. The bench has been this column’s most reliable source for three weeks running. 2-8.

swing_plays.headline: Emmett Johnson’s touchdown flips it again
swing_plays.blurb: The Saturday-morning pickup caught a 6-yard touchdown at 12:28 p.m. for the eighth lead change of a wild Sunday hour, putting Maye I touch your TDs? up 91.62 to 87.82.

swing_plays.headline: Bijan Robinson’s touchdown holds up for 31 hours
swing_plays.blurb: Eight minutes later Robinson scored from 3 yards out and Bad things man bad things led 100.96 to 95.72. It didn’t trail again until Zay Flowers’ catch at 8:09 p.m. Monday, and only for the length of a fumble.

swing_plays.headline: Pickens takes the lead for good
swing_plays.blurb: A week after scoring 0.0, George Pickens caught a 5-yard touchdown at 4:00 p.m. and deeboliciouskins passed Big Stric Energy, 126.48 to 123.24. Big Stric’s day was already over.

swing_plays.headline: Kincaid’s 54 yards put Big Stric in front
swing_plays.blurb: Josh Allen’s deep ball to Dalton Kincaid at 11:59 a.m. was worth 6.4 to Kincaid and 2.16 to Allen, and it flipped the game to Big Stric Energy. It led by 26.58 half an hour later.

swing_plays.headline: McCaffrey’s 74 yards build the 53-point lead
swing_plays.blurb: Christian McCaffrey’s catch-and-run touchdown at 2:34 p.m. put Cherry Blossom up 119.4 to 66.4. Poochinski came back anyway.

features.headline: The trade deadline is next week. Zero trades, ever.
features.dek: Week 11 is the deadline. Three teams have empty QB slots. Four teams have three quarterbacks available. Nobody has ever traded.
body: The R.A.T.S. trade deadline is Week 11. The all-time trade count is 0. I check it every week the way you check a stock you know isn’t moving.

This would be the week. Big Stric Energy, Maye I touch your TDs? and AB81 all project with an empty QB slot. Poochinski, Cherry Blossom, Bad things man bad things and Santa Clara’s Finest each have three quarterbacks available next week. In a two-quarterback league, that is a market. AB81 has empty QB, WR and FLEX slots and projects for 78.28. deeboliciouskins left 46.1 on its bench this week and has depth to spare.
The wire will fill some holes. A trade would fill them better. History says nobody will make one.

features.stat_label: AB81 moves between 4:33 and 4:42 p.m. Sunday
features.headline: AB81 made six moves in nine minutes
features.dek: With the Philadelphia bye gutting the roster, AB81 rebuilt its lineup on Sunday afternoon. Mike Gesicki lasted two minutes.
body: At 4:33 p.m. Sunday, AB81 added Justin Herbert and dropped Joe Milton. At 4:34 p.m., Rico Dowdle for Makai Lemon. At 4:36 p.m., Germie Bernard for Dallas Goedert. At 4:38 p.m., the Cincinnati Bengals D/ST for Darius Cooper. At 4:40 p.m., Mike Gesicki for the Philadelphia Eagles D/ST. At 4:42 p.m., Mark Andrews for Gesicki.
The grades: Herbert 16.26 and Andrews 16.2, both started, both useful. Dowdle 5.4, the Bengals D/ST 5.0, Bernard 1.0. Gesicki scored 1.9, after he’d already been dropped.
It didn’t save the week; AB81 lost by 50.44. And next week is worse: five players on bye and a 78.28 projection. Expect another Sunday-afternoon sprint.

features.headline: Three quarterbacks topped 18 points for nobody
features.dek: Deshaun Watson, Cam Ward and J.J. McCarthy all scored big unrostered, and three R.A.T.S. teams have an empty QB slot.
body: Deebo Samuel Sr. scored 25.9 for nobody, the best unrostered game of the week. Ryan Flournoy (19.1) and Jordyn Tyson (19.0) weren’t far behind.
The quarterbacks matter more. Deshaun Watson 22.38, Cam Ward 20.14, J.J. McCarthy 18.12, all unrostered. Big Stric Energy, Maye I touch your TDs? and AB81 all project with an empty QB slot next week.
The best pickup of the week came off this wire: Emmett Johnson, added by Maye I touch your TDs? at 7:56 a.m. Saturday, scored 35.1. It still lost. The wire can only do so much.

busted.headline: deeboliciouskins starts a bye for its second zero in two weeks
busted.blurb: deeboliciouskins started D’Andre Swift, on bye, for 0.0 while DJ Moore scored 19.4 on its bench. A week ago it started George Pickens, who didn’t play, for 0.0. This time it won by 54.84 over Big Stric Energy, so the zero cost nothing but pride. Two weeks running, though, is a pattern, and the playoffs start in Week 15.

w11-m1.headline: Big Stric Energy gets a short-handed champ
w11-m1.blurb: Big Stric Energy projects for 137.68 to Maye I touch your TDs?’ 106.96 and is a 77.4% favorite. Both have an empty QB slot. Maye has six players on bye and empty QB, TE and DEF slots. Whoever wins the waiver fight for a quarterback wins this game.

w11-m4.headline: Poochinski meets the hottest team in the league
w11-m4.blurb: Poochinski projects for 174.8 and is a 68% favorite over Santa Clara’s Finest at 155.75. Poochinski needs a defense with the Seahawks on bye. The Finest just scored 190.86 and need to keep doing it.

w11-m3.headline: Cherry Blossom favored over the co-leader
w11-m3.blurb: Cherry Blossom projects for 161.15 to Bad things man bad things’ 137.08, a 72.2% edge. Bad things has Golden, Robinson, Charbonnet and its defense on bye and an empty FLEX. Cherry Blossom has no empty slots.

w11-m2.headline: AB81 needs a miracle and a quarterback
w11-m2.blurb: deeboliciouskins projects for 168.98 and AB81 for 78.28, a 90.7-point spread and a 98.7% edge. AB81 has empty QB, WR and FLEX slots. deeboliciouskins needs a kicker and needs to check its byes this time.

playoff_note: Four weeks left, six playoff spots. Poochinski, Bad things man bad things, AB81 and deeboliciouskins are at 100% in the simulations and Cherry Blossom at 99.9%. The top-two race: Poochinski 98.5%, Bad things man bad things 87.7%, Cherry Blossom 7.2%. The fight is for the last spot, and it flipped this week: Santa Clara’s Finest jumped from 5.6% to 57.1%, Maye I touch your TDs? fell from 70.4% to 25.2%, and Big Stric Energy slipped from 25.9% to 17.7%. Big Stric plays Maye next week. Loser is probably done.

waiver_targets.blurb: Scored 20.14 unrostered and projects for 17.09, the best on the wire. Big Stric Energy, Maye I touch your TDs? and AB81 all have an empty QB slot. First claim on the board.
Scored 18.12 for nobody and projects for 15.27. The second quarterback off the board; whoever loses the Ward claim needs him.
Scored 12.8 this week and projects for 11.57. A floor play for the third team that needs a quarterback.
Projects for 13.99. Bad things man bad things has an empty FLEX with Robinson and Charbonnet on bye.
Scored 19.0 unrostered. AB81 has an empty WR slot with Smith-Njigba on bye.

usage_watch.blurb: Opportunities up from 5.1 to 17.5 a game, snap share from 26% to 59%, and 35.1 this week. Maye I touch your TDs? should start him every week.
26.5 opportunities a game over two weeks on an 87% snap share, and 34.2 this week. Bad things man bad things’ best running back right now. Start him.
From 8.0 to 18.5 opportunities on a 72% snap share, projected for 17.05. Cherry Blossom should start him.
Two touchdowns Monday, but 41% of his points come from touchdowns and his opportunities fell from 21.5 to 16.0. AB81 starts him; just don’t count on the floor.
Opportunities down from 16.8 to 9.5 a game and 5.6 this week. Big Stric Energy should bench him.
Opportunities down from 10.3 to 5.5 and a 59% snap share, 3.8 this week. Cherry Blossom can sit him for a hot hand.

rankings.blurb: Erased 53.0, posted the high score, 8-2. The best team in the league.
Won by 0.24 on a fumble. 8-2 and 3-1 in close games. Some call it luck.
Perfect lineup, 46.3 from McCaffrey, still lost. Streak over, team still good.
Won by 54.84 with a bye starter and 46.1 on the bench. Imagine if it tried.
Best score of the season, wire to wire, 57.1% playoff odds. The hottest team in the league.

Lost by 0.24 with 17.5 on the bench. Three straight bench-decided losses.
Led by 26.58, finished with the week’s low score. 2-8.
